subject: Preserve ephemeral logs for HelioPay incident (request from customer)
messages:
From: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@heliopay.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T08:22:00Z
Subject: Production error + logs may have rotated (INC-4321)

Hi Olga,

We're seeing intermittent tokenization failures in payments ingestion that started around 02:00 UTC and we believe the traces that would show the root cause are on your side (model runtime traces + per-request headers). Our retention window for the debug bucket is short and some of the traces have already rotated out.

Can Redwood preserve the relevant ephemeral logs for the next 7 days while our SREs investigate? We can provide sample request IDs and a screenshot of the error (attached). We understand data residency constraints — HelioPay EU customers require data to stay in EU regions.

Ticket: INC-4321
Customer: HelioPay
Requested scope: traces for request IDs 9a3f-*, 9a4b-* (approx 200 requests)
Timeframe: 2026-05-12 01:45 - 03:15 UTC

Please let us know the process and expected TTL for preserved artifacts.

Thanks,
Lena Hoffman
Lead SRE, HelioPay

Attachments:
- heliopay_ticket_4321_screenshots.zip (zip)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production error + logs may have rotated (INC-4321) — request to preserve ephemeral logs

Grace / Rishi — forwarding HelioPay's ask. They explicitly called out EU residency and need us to preserve ~200 request traces for up to 7 days for debugging. They attached screenshots; I've pulled a manifest of the request IDs and attached debug_manifest.json.

Key constraints:
- Region: eu-central (customer says EU-only)
- Scope: request IDs 9a3f-* and 9a4b-* (I filtered by request prefix, ~200 entries)
- Timebox: 7 days from 2026-05-12 (customer requested)

Ask: Marcus — can infra apply a short TTL override on the specific bucket/prefix (eu-customer/heliopay/inc-4321/) or snapshot those objects into a retention hold area?
Rishi / Grace — need compliance sign-off. If we proceed, we should:
  * limit access to SREs working on INC-4321
  * set a hard expiry (automated deletion)
  * record approval in Jira (INC-4321) and in the retention-exceptions log

I think a short (<=7d) scoped hold with narrow ACLs is reasonable but want to ensure legal/security OK given EU residency.

Attachments: debug_manifest.json (application/json)

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production error + logs may have rotated (INC-4321) — request to preserve ephemeral logs

Thanks for the context, Olga.

Principles: we can approve very narrow, timebound exceptions for live incidents where customer impact is high and root cause requires data that would otherwise be lost — provided we follow an approval checklist. For EU data we must ensure no cross-border copies are created.

Rishi — please advise if you'd be comfortable with the following minimal controls:
- Approval recorded on INC-4321 with explicit justification and expiry (7 days)
- Preserve only the exact prefixes in the manifest (do not widen scope)
- ACL: read-by-owner + SRE list only; no external backups or transfers out of eu-central
- Audit: record access events and notify compliance after deletion

Marcus — if infra can snapshot to a temporary retention-bucket in eu-central with the above ACLs and automated deletion on 2026-05-19T09:00:00Z, I will mark this as approved from a support/manager perspective pending Rishi's security ok.

Also, please ensure we redact any PII if found in traces before sharing with HelioPay SREs (they will get scoped access).

Grace O'Connor
Support Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production error + logs may have rotated (INC-4321) — security sign-off (conditional)

I agree with Grace's controls, with two additional conditions before infra executes:
1) Acceptance: HelioPay must confirm in writing that the data will be used solely for root-cause analysis for INC-4321 and will not be exported. We should capture that confirmation in the Jira ticket.
2) Scope verification: Marcus or Olga should provide a short report listing object keys to be preserved (count, total size, prefixes). I see the manifest attached but prefer a quick verification step to avoid over-preserving.

If both items are satisfied, security gives a conditional sign-off for a 7-day, eu-only snapshot with the ACLs Grace listed. Please document the approval and schedule the automated deletion.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@heliopay.com>
Date: 2026-05-15T16:40:00Z
Subject: Action: snapshot + confirmation to HelioPay (INC-4321)

Marcus — going ahead with the snapshot now per approvals. Summary:
- Snapshot target: eu-customer/heliopay/inc-4321-snap-20260515
- Objects: prefixes 9a3f-*, 9a4b-* (manifest attached) — 197 objects, ~280 MB total
- ACL: rw for infra + scoped SRE group; denied for backups/export services
- Expiry: automated deletion scheduled for 2026-05-22T09:00:00Z (7 days from snapshot)
- Security conditions: HelioPay confirmation in Jira (INC-4321) attached; audit logging enabled

Lena — FYI I've given HelioPay scoped access to the snapshot (EU region only). Please confirm you accept the limited use and expiry so we can close the approval loop in the ticket. We will delete the snapshot automatically on 2026-05-22T09:00:00Z unless you request an extension and provide additional justification.

Attachments: debug_manifest.json (application/json)

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Support Engineer, Redwood Inference
